title: Removing one coordinate gives a short exact kernel sequence with ideal quotient
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I a finite type of indices, and p:O_X^(Option I) → O_X a sheaf-module morphism [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put q=freeMap(some) followed by p. There exist ideal sheaf data J with J.toModules quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and a short exact sequence kernel q → kernel p → J.toModules. No surjectivity of p is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering, paragraph constructing F_i as the intersection with the first i direct summands; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XF

proof.text: Let inc include the coordinates indexed by I, let r discard the none coordinate, let t project onto that coordinate, and let s include it. Construct r and t as coproduct descents. Coproduct extensionality proves inc followed by r is identity, inc followed by t is zero, and r followed by inc plus t followed by s is identity. In particular inc is mono. Let a:kernel q → kernel p be the induced kernel map and v:kernel p → O_X be the projection t after the kernel inclusion. Then a is mono and a followed by v is zero.

For any k:T → kernel p killed by v, the splitting identity gives k followed by the kernel inclusion, r and inc equal to k followed by the kernel inclusion. Thus k followed by the kernel inclusion and r is killed by q; kernel.lift q provides its unique factorization through a. Cancellation of the mono kernel inclusion proves the factorization identity. This is the universal property of kernel v, formalized with KernelFork.IsLimit.ofι'.

The free source and unit module are quasi-coherent, so kernel p is quasi-coherent. Apply cokernel closure to v and kernel closure to its cokernel projection. Abelian.image v is by definition that kernel, so it is quasi-coherent. Apply quasiCoherent_submodule_ideal to the image inclusion to obtain J and an isomorphism from the image to J.toModules.

The factorization b0:kernel p → image v is epi. Since the image inclusion is mono, cancel it to prove a followed by b0 is zero, and use isKernelOfComp to retain the kernel universal property. ShortComplex.exact_of_f_is_kernel gives exactness; mono a and epi b0 give short exactness. Transport this sequence along the isomorphism image v ≅ J.toModules using ShortComplex.isoMk and shortExact_of_iso.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_free_kernel_coordinate_step (X : Scheme.{u})
    {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    (p : SheafOfModules.free (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (Option I) ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) :
    ∃ J : X.IdealSheafData, J.toModules.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ∃ (a : kernel (SheafOfModules.freeMap (R := X.ringCatSheaf) some ≫ p) ⟶ kernel p)
        (b : kernel p ⟶ J.toModules) (w : a ≫ b = 0),
        (ShortComplex.mk a b w).ShortExact
